findings.title: immediateDelete path leaves the WorkflowReminder row in the DB
findings.body: In `deleteScheduledEmailReminder`, when `immediateDelete` is true the function cancels the scheduled send at SendGrid and returns without deleting (or updating) the `workflowReminder` row. Callers that use this path (handleNewBooking reschedule, workflows.tsx workflow/step deletion) therefore leave orphaned reminder rows with `scheduled: true` and a now-unusable `referenceId`. The row lingers until the cron's `deleteMany(scheduledDate <= now)` eventually removes it, and because `referenceId` is `@unique` a stale row can also block reuse. The non-immediate path at least marks `cancelled: true`; the immediate path should delete the row.

findings.title: Reschedule path still uses immediate SendGrid cancellation, so the bug being fixed persists for reschedules
findings.body: The PR's stated fix is to avoid SendGrid's 100-pending-cancellation limit by deferring cancellation to the cron (`cancelled: true`). However the reschedule path calls `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId, true)` with `immediateDelete = true`, which issues the `POST /v3/user/scheduled_sends` cancel immediately. Reschedules will therefore keep accumulating pending cancellations and can still fail once the limit is reached, meaning reminders for rescheduled bookings are still sent — exactly the reported issue (#7225) for the reschedule case. The same applies to workflow/step deletion in workflows.tsx.

findings.title: Single SendGrid failure aborts cancellation of all remaining reminders
findings.body: The cancellation loop is wrapped in one `try/catch` and `await`s the SendGrid request inside the loop. If any single `client.request` throws (e.g. invalid/expired batch_id, rate limit), the catch is hit and all remaining `remindersToCancel` in this run are skipped. Since the cancellation window is only 1 hour and the cron runs every 15 minutes, repeated failures on the same bad reminder will permanently prevent later reminders in the list from being cancelled, and their emails will be sent. The try/catch should be per-reminder inside the loop.

findings.title: Cancellation query is not restricted to EMAIL reminders or non-null referenceId
findings.body: `remindersToCancel` selects every `workflowReminder` with `cancelled: true` and `scheduledDate <= now+1h`, without filtering `method: WorkflowMethods.EMAIL` or `referenceId: { not: null }`. Any non-email or reference-less row that ends up with `cancelled: true` would be sent to the SendGrid scheduled_sends endpoint with a null/foreign batch_id, which errors and (per the finding above) aborts the whole batch.

findings.title: Unscheduled-reminder query does not exclude cancelled reminders
findings.body: The `unscheduledReminders` query filters on `method: EMAIL, scheduled: false` but not `cancelled`. A reminder that was scheduled far in the future (stored with `scheduled: false`) and then cancelled on booking cancellation/reschedule will still be picked up by this cron and scheduled with SendGrid, so a reminder for a cancelled booking gets sent. Add `cancelled: null` / `not: true` to the where clause (or delete such rows).

findings.title: PrismaPromise imported as a runtime value
findings.body: The import was changed from `import type { Prisma, PrismaPromise }` to a value import that includes `PrismaPromise`. `PrismaPromise` (and `Prisma` as used here) are type-only exports of @prisma/client; importing them in a value import can fail at build/runtime with isolatedModules/SWC transpilation ("PrismaPromise is not exported"). Keep these as `import type`.

findings.title: Reminder cancellation promises are not awaited
findings.body: `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` / `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` are async but invoked inside `forEach` without awaiting; the handler returns a 200 "Booking successfully cancelled" before the `cancelled: true` DB updates complete. In a serverless environment the function may be frozen/terminated before the updates are persisted, leaving reminders uncancelled. Collect the promises and `await Promise.all`.

findings.title: try/catch cannot catch failures of the un-awaited async calls
findings.body: The `try { originalRescheduledBooking.workflowReminders.forEach(... deleteScheduledEmailReminder(...)) } catch` block cannot catch errors from these promises since they are not awaited; a rejection would surface as an unhandled rejection rather than the intended `log.error`. Await the promises inside the try.
